learning_outcomes.text: To show the important role played by different individuals, peoples and cultures in human history.
To determine the structuring of individuals' relationships with each other in terms of cultural concepts.
To document people's thoughts, intellectual knowledge and contributions in the historical process.
To ensure the sustainability of individuals' relationships with philosophy, science, literature and art throughout their lives.

syllabus_topics: What is Civilization? How do Civilizations form?
Prehistoric Ages and Historic Ages and Civilizations
New discoveries and colonialism: Asia, Africa and America, the achievements of the twentieth century: quests in science, art and philosophy
Globalization, New Colonialism and Imperialism Discussions
assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course schedule. Midterm and final exam dates are held on the dates specified in the academic calendar by the decision of the University Senate.
